review.alternative: Full system state information could potentially provide tighter bounds than trajectory-observable inference.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence that trajectory-observable inference systematically fails in high-dimensional chaotic systems.

claims.statement: Trajectory-level entropy production can be lower-bounded using only observable spatiotemporal correlations, bypassing the need for full high-dimensional state reconstruction.

support.explanation: Establishes a methodology for lower-bounding dissipation without requiring full system state information.
support.passage: We infer trajectory-level EP and lower bounds on average EP by exploiting a nonequilibrium analogue of the Maximum Entropy principle, along with convex duality. Our approach uses only samples of trajectory observables, such as spatiotemporal correlations. It does not require reconstruction of high-dimensional probability distributions or rate matrices

review.alternative: Upper bounds might be significantly looser if hidden, passive degrees of freedom are strongly coupled to the driven particles.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence showing that passive degrees of freedom increase dissipation beyond the driving-statistics bound.

claims.statement: Entropy production rates in overdamped Langevin systems can be upper-bounded by considering the statistics of the driven particles alone.

support.explanation: Provides a robust analytical upper bound on dissipation based on particle driving statistics.
support.passage: For particles in a thermal environment and driven by non-conservative forces, we show that the entropy production rate can be upper bounded by considering only the statistics of the driven particles.

actions.findings:
Trajectory-level entropy production can be lower-bounded using only observable spatiotemporal correlations, bypassing the need for full high-dimensional state reconstruction. [source-dc0bb1a28c9b4193]

Entropy production rates in overdamped Langevin systems can be upper-bounded by considering the statistics of the driven particles alone. [peer-de432c24032230d8b2f550f3]
actions.limitations: Inferences rely on the availability of trajectory observables (like spatiotemporal correlations) rather than full microscopic state information. Theoretical bounds for Langevin dynamics assume overdamped conditions, limiting applicability in high-inertia regimes.
actions.next_questions: Can these trajectory-based entropy production bounds be directly mapped to the memory requirements of information engines, or do they remain distinct from the information-theoretic costs of state-switching?
actions.reason: Incorporating new nonequilibrium entropy production inference techniques to refine dissipation bounds.
actions.summary: This revision incorporates trajectory-based inference of entropy production and Langevin-derived upper bounds, refining our understanding of how limited state information constrains thermodynamic dissipation estimation.
actions.title: Refined Coarse-Grained Dissipation Bounds and Finite Relaxation
